newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels free 41 in assault on prison.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels free 41 in assault on prison.

text.p: Leftist rebels freed 41 prisoners, some of them fellow guerrillas, in a raid on a jail in the capital of Colombia's jungle-covered southwest province of Putumayo, authorities said on Saturday.

Police and military officials said the attack by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels occurred at dawn on Friday and that only seven of the 41 inmates sprung from the prison in Mocoa, the Putumayo capital, had been caught as of Saturday afternoon.

An undetermined number of the prisoners released in the assault were rebels from the Putumayo area, where the FARC launched a dramatic offensive in late August in which dozens of security force members were killed and at least 60 taken prisoner.

In other developments, military sources said up to 15 guerrillas and one soldier were killed in fighting early on Saturday in a rural area of Norte de Santander province, near Colombia's border with Venezuela.
At least 25 people were wounded in the fighting, which was the bloodiest reported anywhere in the country since last month, the sources said.

In central Meta province, meanwhile, just east of the Colombia capital, FARC rebels held up an armoured car early on Saturday and made off with the equivalent of more than $6,000 after killing its driver in a shootout.

The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, was founded as a pro-Soviet Marxist group in the early 1960s. Its roots go back to the peasant militias that operated across Colombia in the late 1940s.
